native.summary: Capillaries up close. Left, to scale: an arteriole feeding a metarteriole, precapillary sphincters at the mouths of the true capillaries (arterial to venous, red to blue, red cells in single file), the thoroughfare channel into the venule, an arteriovenous anastomosis (glomus) bypassing the bed, and a blind-ended lymphatic capillary with overlapping endothelial flaps and anchoring filaments draining into a valved lymphatic vessel. Right, 3 times larger: continuous, fenestrated and sinusoidal capillaries cut lengthwise.
native.scale_note: The capillary network is drawn to scale in micrometres (capillaries 8 µm, red cells 7.5 µm, arteriole 30 µm, venule 26 µm, lymphatic capillary about 18 µm). The three capillary types on the right are magnified 3 times, and their fenestrae are enlarged further so they can be seen; the ruler applies to the network only. Both regions are cut through the middle so the walls and lumens show.

Whole model.note: Left: one capillary network to scale, cut through its middle. Right: the three capillary types, 3 times larger.

Capillary network.note: Arteriole → metarteriole → arterial capillaries → venous capillaries → venule, with the thoroughfare channel straight through, an AV anastomosis over the top and a lymphatic capillary below.

Metarteriole and precapillary sphincters.note: The metarteriole leaves the arteriole; a ring of smooth muscle (precapillary sphincter) guards the mouth of each true capillary.

Thoroughfare channel and venule.note: The metarteriole runs straight on as the thoroughfare channel into the venule: consistent flow, even with the sphincters shut.

True capillaries and red cells.note: Capillaries 7-9 µm wide carry red cells in single file; the colour runs from arterial red to venous blue.

Arteriovenous anastomosis (glomus).note: A thick, muscular arteriovenous anastomosis (glomus) shunts blood from the arteriole straight to the venule, skipping the capillaries.

Lymphatic capillary.note: A blind-ended lymphatic capillary: overlapping endothelial cells act as one-way flaps, and anchoring filaments tie it to the collagen.

Lymphatic vessel valve.note: The collecting lymphatic vessel and its two-leaflet valve: lymph moves one way only.

Three capillary types (3x).note: Continuous (top), fenestrated (middle) and sinusoidal (bottom) capillaries, cut lengthwise and shown 3 times larger.

Continuous capillary.note: Continuous: cells joined with no gaps and no fenestrae, a complete basement membrane, and a pericyte outside.

Fenestrated capillary.note: Fenestrated: thin cells full of windows (fenestrae, enlarged here), still joined with no gaps, on a complete basement membrane.

Sinusoidal capillary.note: Sinusoidal: wide, with large fenestrae, gaps between the cells, only patches of basement membrane, and a macrophage in the lining.

viewer.scale_note: The capillary network is drawn to scale in micrometres (capillaries 8 µm, red cells 7.5 µm, arteriole 30 µm, venule 26 µm, lymphatic capillary about 18 µm). The three capillary types on the right are magnified 3 times, and their fenestrae are enlarged further so they can be seen; the ruler applies to the network only. Both regions are cut through the middle so the walls and lumens show.

parts.name: Arteriole: tunica intima (endothelium)
parts.description: Inner layer of the arteriole: endothelium (simple squamous) on its basement membrane, with the internal elastic membrane outside it.

parts.name: Arteriole: tunica media (smooth muscle)
parts.description: Arteriole (9-40 µm), the smallest artery in which all three tunics can still be told apart. Its circular smooth muscle constricts and dilates it, which is how it controls flow into the capillary network.

parts.name: Arteriole: tunica externa
parts.description: Thin connective-tissue outer coat (tunica externa) of the arteriole.

parts.name: Metarteriole
parts.description: Metarteriole: a short vessel from the arteriole that still has some smooth muscle. It feeds the true capillaries and continues straight on as the thoroughfare channel. Path: arteriole → metarteriole → arterial capillaries → venous capillaries → venule.

parts.name: Metarteriole: smooth muscle cells
parts.description: Scattered smooth muscle cells around the metarteriole (no longer a continuous media).

parts.name: Precapillary sphincters
parts.description: Precapillary sphincters: rings of smooth muscle on the metarteriole at the mouth of each true capillary. They open and close to regulate blood flow into the capillary network, so flow through the true capillaries is intermittent.

parts.name: Arterial capillaries
parts.description: Arterial (first) half of the true capillaries, 7-9 µm wide. The wall is endothelium, basement membrane and a delicate layer of loose connective tissue. Red cells pass in single file. Fluid tends to leave the capillary at this end, pushed out by blood pressure.

parts.name: Venous capillaries
parts.description: Venous (second) half of the true capillaries, draining to the venule. Most of the fluid that left at the arterial end returns here; what remains in the tissue is taken up by the lymphatic capillaries. The colour runs from arterial red to venous blue as oxygen is given up.

parts.name: Thoroughfare channel
parts.description: Thoroughfare channel: the metarteriole continuing directly into the venule. Flow through it to the venule is consistent (always on), even when the precapillary sphincters are shut. Skin has more of these channels (thermoregulation).

parts.name: Venule
parts.description: Venule (up to 50 µm): drains the capillary network. Endothelium and basement membrane with a few smooth muscle cells; more muscle as venules get bigger. Passes blood to small veins.

parts.name: Venule: smooth muscle cells
parts.description: A few smooth muscle cells around the venule wall; their number grows as venules get larger.

parts.name: AV anastomosis: endothelium
parts.description: Endothelial lining of the arteriovenous anastomosis.

parts.name: AV anastomosis (glomus): smooth muscle
parts.description: Arteriovenous anastomosis: a direct connection from the arteriole to the venule that skips the capillaries. A glomus is an AV anastomosis with abundant smooth muscle in its wall; glomera regulate body temperature and are abundant in the sole, palm, terminal phalanges and nail beds.

parts.name: Lymphatic capillary: overlapping endothelial cells
parts.description: Lymphatic capillary: blind-ended, more permeable than a blood capillary and without a basement membrane. Its endothelial cells overlap like shingles: interstitial fluid pushes the free edges inward and enters, and pressure inside pushes them shut, so the cells act as one-way valves. The fluid is now lymph.

parts.name: Anchoring filaments
parts.description: Anchoring filaments tie the lymphatic capillary to the surrounding collagen. When tissue fluid builds up and the tissue swells, they pull the capillary open.

parts.name: Collecting lymphatic vessel
parts.description: Lymphatic vessel formed by joining lymphatic capillaries. Its structure is similar to a small vein, and it carries lymph away from the tissues toward nodes, trunks and ducts.

parts.name: Lymphatic vessel valve
parts.description: Valve of a lymphatic vessel: two leaflets that let lymph pass in one direction only. Valves divide the vessel into chambers that pump when their smooth muscle contracts.

parts.name: Lymphocytes in the lymph
parts.description: Lymphocytes carried in the lymph toward the lymph nodes.

parts.name: Red blood cells
parts.description: Red blood cells (about 7.5 µm). In the 7-9 µm capillaries they pass one at a time and fold into a cup; in the arteriole and venule they tumble freely.

parts.name: Pericytes (pericapillary cells)
parts.description: Pericapillary cells (pericytes) wrapped around the capillary wall: the scattered cells the lecture lists as fibroblasts, macrophages or undifferentiated smooth muscle cells.

parts.name: Fibroblasts
parts.description: Fibroblasts of the loose connective tissue around the capillary network.

parts.name: Macrophage
parts.description: A tissue macrophage in the connective tissue between the vessels.

parts.name: Collagen fibres
parts.description: Collagen fibres of the connective tissue, behind the network. The lymphatic capillary is anchored to them.

parts.name: Cell nuclei
parts.description: Nuclei of the pericytes, fibroblasts, macrophage and lymphocytes.

parts.name: Continuous capillary: endothelial cells
parts.description: Continuous capillary (muscle, nervous tissue and many other sites): the endothelial cells join edge to edge with no gaps and no fenestrae, so it is the least permeable to large molecules. Substances cross through the cells or the narrow clefts between them.

parts.name: Continuous capillary: cell junctions
parts.description: Junctions sealing the clefts between neighbouring endothelial cells: no gaps.

parts.name: Continuous capillary: basement membrane
parts.description: Complete basement membrane around the continuous capillary.

parts.name: Continuous capillary: pericyte
parts.description: A pericapillary cell (pericyte) on the outside of the basement membrane.

parts.name: Fenestrated capillary: endothelial cells
parts.description: Fenestrated capillary (intestinal villi, ciliary process of the eye, choroid plexus, glomeruli of the kidney): thin endothelial cells with numerous fenestrae, windows where the cytoplasm is absent and the plasma membrane is thin and porous. Highly permeable. Fenestrae are drawn larger than life so they can be seen.

parts.name: Fenestrated capillary: cell junctions
parts.description: Junctions between the fenestrated capillary’s endothelial cells: still no gaps between the cells.

parts.name: Fenestrated capillary: basement membrane
parts.description: Continuous basement membrane around the fenestrated capillary.

parts.name: Sinusoidal capillary: endothelial cells
parts.description: Sinusoidal capillary (liver, endocrine glands): large diameter, large fenestrae and wide gaps between the endothelial cells, so even large molecules and cells can pass.

parts.name: Sinusoidal capillary: basement membrane
parts.description: Less basement membrane: only patches around the sinusoid.

parts.name: Sinusoidal capillary: macrophage
parts.description: A macrophage in the sinusoid lining (in the liver, a Kupffer cell) that cleans debris from the slow, leaky blood.

parts.name: Endothelial and other nuclei (3x)
parts.description: Nuclei of the endothelial cells (bulging into the lumen), the pericyte and the macrophage.

parts.name: Red blood cells (3x)
parts.description: Red blood cells for scale: they just fit the continuous and fenestrated capillaries and float loosely in the wide sinusoid.
